properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 5 at 7:42PM EDT until September 5 at 9:30PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...West Central Carteret County in eastern North Carolina...
Southeastern Craven County in eastern North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 930 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Overflowing poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 742 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.1 to 0.5 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Havelock, Morehead City, Newport, North River, Harlowe, Wildwood,
North Harlowe, Michael J Smith Airport, Crab Point Village and
Mitchell Village.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:
ESFMSO

What: Widespread moderate rainfall over a prolonged period of time.
Storm total amounts between 1 to 3 inches for valleys and 2 to 3
inches for the mountains.  There is a 10 percent chance of isolated
rainfall amounts up to 4 inches along the Continental Divide.

Where: Flathead and Lake Counties in northwest Montana, including
Glacier National Park. Missoula county in west-central Montana.

Timing: Beginning Sunday morning, continuing through Monday night.
Heaviest rainfall rates anticipated Monday into Monday night.

Significant rainfall totals will bring potential for rapid rises on
streams and creeks, rock and debris slides and runoff issues in poor
drainage areas. Those recreating in the backcountry should take
caution on backcountry roadways for falling debris.

Mountain Front and then spread eastward out over the plains of North
Central MT by Sunday night.

North Central MT from Sunday through Monday, including the east side
of Glacier Park. There is a 10 percent chance of isolated rainfall
amounts up to 4 inches.

that do receive closer to 3 inches or more of rainfall, some minor
field or small stream flooding can not be ruled out. Additionally,
some rocks could wash down on to roadways near mountains.

Those planning outdoor activities over the next few days should be
prepared for periods of rain.

* WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties,
especially for south-facing beaches including the Lost Coast
Trail.

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach
without warning, sweeping people into the sea from rocks,
jetties, and beaches. These sneaker waves can also move large
objects such as logs, crushing anyone caught underneath.

30 minutes of small waves before a sneaker wave strikes.  Avoid
rocks and jetties. Avoid steep beaches.  Stay much farther back
from the water and never turn your back on the ocean.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued September 5 at 2:13AM CDT until September 8 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Topeka KS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with afternoon heat index values
of 100 to 108.

* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central, and
northeast Kansas.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM CDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat and high humidity events.
properties.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 4 at 9:24PM PDT until September 8 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 5 to 8 feet with local sets to 10 feet and dangerous
and potentially life threatening rip currents, largest on
south- facing shores.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Saturday to 11 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents will be widespread and very strong, potentially
pulling swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves
can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and
capsize small boats near shore. Enhanced beach erosion will
occur. Flooding of sea water is likely, around the time of
high tide, over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas such as
parking lots, beaches, and walkways. Areas most susceptible to
coastal flooding will include Avalon, Long Beach (Alamitos
Peninsula), and Oxnard to Malibu (including Point Mugu).

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides at 6.3 feet will occur around
5pm on Saturday, 6.7 feet at 6pm on Sunday, 7 feet at 7pm on
Monday, and 7.2 feet at 8pm on Tuesday.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks. Follow advice from local
officials. Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.
